saints.name: St. Dominic of Silos
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: A Spanish abbot who rebuilt the monastery of Silos and was long invoked by mothers and by captives…
biography: Born about the year 1000 at Cañas in Navarre, Dominic kept his father's flocks as a boy before entering the Benedictine monastery of San Millán de la Cogolla, where he rose to be prior. Refusing King García Sánchez III of Navarre the surrender of the monastery's lands, he was driven into exile with two of his brethren.

Ferdinand I of Castile and León received the exiles, and in 1041 set Dominic over the decayed monastery of Saint Sebastian at Silos, where only six monks remained. Under his rule Silos was renewed in cloister and scriptorium until it stood among the renowned houses of Spain, and the abbot grew famous for his works of healing and for ransoming Christian captives from the Moors.

He died at Silos on 20 December 1073. A century later Joan of Aza prayed at his tomb for a child and bore the son she named Dominic — the future founder of the Friars Preachers. For that grace he is invoked by expectant mothers, and his abbatial staff was long laid by the queens of Spain in their labor; for his own youth and his ransoms he is the patron of shepherds and of captives.
saints.knownFor: Restorer of the abbey of Silos and helper of captives and mothers.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 20 December
